_about: Baron d'Holbach (1723-1789), materialist of the French Enlightenment: The System of Nature, with notes by Diderot, tr. H. D. Robinson, two volumes in one (Boston: J. P. Mendum, 1868; raw IA OCR), and Good Sense, from Le Bon Sens, translator unnamed (London: W. Stewart, undated, c. 1900 by the Gutenberg transcriber's note; clean Gutenberg text). Held: Gutenberg's System of Nature (8909-8910), a modern facsimile of the 1820-21 translation (now held above from the period printing), and Ecce Homo (39052), a 1977 facsimile. Letters to Eugenia is on Lane C's ac-middleton. Added in round ao: The System of Nature, or the Laws of the Moral and Physical World, 'translated from the original French of M. de Mirabaud', 3 vols. in one scan (London: Thomas Davison, 1820; R. Helder, 1821), the anonymous 1820-21 translation in its period printing. US public domain. No uids minted.

holbach-good-sense-c1900: Good Sense, a translation of Le Bon Sens (London: W. Stewart, undated, c. 1900)

holbach-robinson-system-of-nature-1868: The System of Nature, with notes by Diderot, two volumes in one (Boston: J. P. Mendum, 1868)
holbach-system-of-nature-1820-21: The System of Nature, or the Laws of the Moral and Physical World, 'translated from the original French of M. de Mirabaud', 3 vols. in one scan (London: Thomas Davison, 1820; R. Helder, 1821)

holbach-system-of-nature-1820-21.author: The title page names 'M. de Mirabaud', the pseudonym under which d'Holbach published the Systeme de la nature (1770); the 1820-21 Davison/Helder translation is the one Gutenberg's facsimile reproduces.
